transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-02-14 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Talia Nguyen (Redwood SE), Jordan Reed (CTO, Acme), Mina Alvarez (Lead ML Eng), Samuel Price (Security)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on multi-tenant controls: org vs project keys, rate limiting/quotas, tenant isolation patterns, sticky routing and routing by policy. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated for latency and compliance. Agreed next steps: send pricing matrix, VPC checklist, schedule POC scoping.

Topics covered:
- Org/project key semantics and recommended setup for Acme (internal teams + external partners)
- Quota strategies: per-org, per-project, per-key concurrency caps and token quotas
- Sticky routing & fairshare: routing to dedicated pools when reserved capacity is present
- RBAC, audit logs, KMS integrations, and SAML/SSO considerations for Private deployments
- Optimize suggestions: batching, prefix/KV cache, quantization recommendations for cost targets

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on. We got about 55 minutes, why don't we start with a quick context check. Jordan, can you give us a 30-second on what you're trying to solve?
[00:12] Jordan: Sure. We're Acme MedTech, trying to embed LLM features in our clinical workflow product. Low latency is important for the UI — ideally sub 100ms server-side for single-turn queries. We also need strict tenant isolation because we've got multi-tenant hospitals and partner integrations.
[00:28] Mina: And from engineering, we want a clear quota model so that development teams and partners can't blast through our bill. We're also evaluating dedicated capacity vs hosted.
[00:36] Samir: Perfect. Talia will walk through the console and the org/project key model, then we'll demo quota and routing policies.
[00:44] Talia: Alright. In Redwood the highest-level object is an org, you can then carve projects which map to product teams or external tenants. Each project gets project keys. We recommend one org per company and then projects for each external customer if you want billing separation.
[00:60] Jordan: Quick question — if we use project keys for partners, can we enforce different quotas per key?
[01:07] Talia: Yes, you can apply quota slices at the key level: token caps, concurrency, and burst windows. For example you could do 10k tokens/day per partner key, and a concurrency cap of 3 concurrent requests.
[01:22] Mina: How does that play with org-level reserved capacity? Say we buy a Dedicated pool for peak traffic — do partner keys get routed there automatically?
[01:31] Talia: You can do policy-driven routing. There's a priority order: first-match policy can route specific project keys to Dedicated pools. If the dedicated pool is at capacity, you can configure fallback to hosted or a lower-cost quantized variant. We call this sticky routing in the console — it keeps a key consistently routed to the same capacity for cache locality.
[01:52] Samuel: From a security angle we need audit logs and KMS support. Does the Private deployment allow HSM-backed keys?
[02:01] Samir: Yes. For Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. We'll share the security whitepaper, but the quick answer is yes, and you can restrict key creation via RBAC and SSO.
[02:14] Mina: A nit: sometimes the docs mention KV cache and prefix cache. How does that interact with project-level routing? If a partner is on different pool, do they lose caching benefits?
[02:26] Talia: Good point. The runtime keeps KV/prefix caches local to the serving pool. That's why sticky routing matters — if you route a partner consistently to the dedicated pool they'll keep hot KV cache and prefix cache warm, which preserves low-latency for follow-up requests. If you bounce them across pools you'll lose that benefit and see higher tail latencies.
[02:45] Jordan: What's the recommended setup for our use-case — small number of large tenants, plus internal dev teams?
[02:51] Talia: For that pattern we suggest a hybrid: Dedicated pools for the largest tenants (top 3 hospitals), hosted for internal and low-volume partners. Use project keys for tenants and org-level quota for global spend limits. Also set per-key concurrency to protect the Dedicated pool from noisy tenants.
[03:07] Jordan: How strict are rate-limit enforcement windows — do you round on per-second or per-minute?
[03:12] Talia: We support millisecond-level token accounting internally but quotas expose windows at second/minute/hour/day depending on policy type. For concurrency it's instant; for token quotas you can do rolling windows or fixed windows.
[03:23] Mina: Can we do fairshare across projects? Like make sure one partner doesn't starve others if they share the same dedicated pool?
[03:29] Samir: Yep — fairshare policies let you assign weight per project key within a pool so the scheduler enforces proportional throughput. It plays nicely with concurrency caps and burst buffers.
[03:40] Jordan: Any hard limits we should know about for Dedicated — like max concurrent requests per GPU?
[03:46] Talia: Depends on model and batch config. For smaller LLMs you might get hundreds of concurrent tiny requests per GPU with continuous batching; for large transformer models concurrency is lower. Talia: We'll run a quick estimate for your model mix.
[03:57] Mina: Can you show the console UI for setting a policy?
[04:00] Talia: Sure — pulling up the console. (screen share noise) Here is a policy editor: route by org/project key, priority, fallback, and target pool. You can also attach quota objects and alerts.
[04:15] (minor audio garble)
[04:18] Talia: I'm creating a demo rule: project key = acme-hospital-west -> DedicatedPool-West, concurrency cap = 4, token quota = 500k/day, fallback = hosted-quantized. Note the UI warns if fallback increases expected latency.
[04:34] Jordan: Is there a way to simulate a noisy key to see eviction behavior?
[04:39] Talia: Yes, we have a live test harness — you can run a load generator against a test key and watch request routing, evictions, and metrics in the dashboard. We'll include access in the POC.
[04:50] Samir: Let's touch on billing segmentation. You said you wanted partner-level chargeback?
[04:55] Jordan: Correct. We'd like to bill some partners directly and absorb internal usage.
[04:59] Samir: Use org-level billing if everything's on one account; for pass-through billing you can create sub-orgs or export per-key usage to your billing pipeline. We also support per-project cost centers in the console so you can allocate spend to different internal teams.
[05:12] Mina: On compliance — retention windows for logs and transcripts?
[05:16] Samir: Hosted defaults to 30 days for non-PHI data, but with enterprise add-ons you can increase retention or opt for Private with your own retention policies. For PHI you should use Private or specific BAA workflows — we'll send the compliance note.
[05:30] Samuel: Does Redwood have SOC 2?
[05:32] Samir: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, and we can share the report under an NDA.
[05:36] Jordan: Can we pin a model version per project key so a partner always sees the same model?
[05:40] Talia: Yes — model pinning is supported per-route. You can pin to a specific model and quantization profile so rollouts are deterministic. We also version models in the catalog for auditability.
[05:50] Mina: If we pin to a quantized variant for cost reasons, can we set quality gates? Like auto-roll back if evals degrade?
[05:56] Samir: Redwood Optimize hooks into evals and quality monitors; you can set regression alerts on prompt sets. We can demo that in the POC.
[06:02] Jordan: Ok, last questions — how do we get started with the POC?
[06:06] Samir: We'll send a POC scoping agenda. Typical items: target tenants, sample traffic, success criteria (latency, cost per 1k tokens, uptime), and timeline. We'll also provide a temporary dedicated pool estimate and pricing.
[06:18] Mina: For the POC, can we get a VPC/private control plane access?
[06:22] Samir: We can do a Private eval or a Hosted with VPC peering depending on your needs. We'll include both options in the doc.
[06:29] (overlap) Jordan: Great.
[06:31] Samir: Cool — recap of next steps: we'll send the pricing + SLA, VPC checklist, and schedule the POC scoping. Talia will run the latency/cost estimate.
[06:41] Jordan: Perfect thanks.
[06:42] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD with links.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "sticky routing" was sometimes transcribed as "sticky routing" or "sticker routing" in the console. Company product references: Redwood Optimize / Redwood Dedicated sometimes appear in transcript as "Redwood Optimae" or "Red wood dedicated" — these are transcription artifacts.
